Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

develop verb

a talent, a skill, a plan

also cultivate, build up, work out, devise, come up with

classical

Cic. Arch. 12: animōs doctrīnā (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Tr. 4.10.15: prōtinus excolimur tenerī

excolō, excolere, excoluī, excultum

verb, third conjugation

develop, cultivate, refine

Of people, minds and talents: to train and refine them.

Other words

  • alō, alere, aluī, altum (alitum) — feed, foster (a talent)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 45: ingenium industriā alitur (Lewis & Short); Cic. Off. 1.105: hominis autem mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō

    A talent grows on what feeds it.

  • excōgitō, excōgitāre, excōgitāvī, excōgitātum — devise, think out

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plin. NH 15.82: nūper excōgitātum est

    Of a new plan, method or thing: to develop a recipe, a game, a program.

Examples

  • prōtinus excolimur tenerī cūrāque parentis īmus ad īnsignēs urbis ab arte virōs

    from our earliest years we were schooled, and by our father’s care we went to the men of the city famous for their artOv. Tr. 4.10.15–16

  • hominis autem mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō

    the human mind is fed by learning and thinkingCic. Off. 1.105

  • cum recentī fīcō salis vice cāseō vescī nūper excōgitātum est

    eating cheese with fresh figs instead of salt is a recent inventionPlin. NH 15.82

See also develop, practice.
